investigation.title: Remote Agents: Swarm Gateway 502 — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing via Shared ELB Dependency
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-16T01:22–01:23Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm provisioning gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2) was unreachable when POST /api/agents was called. Because every check shares the same error message and the upstream POST /api/agents call is the first step for all three, the failure is localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual check's logic.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS Elastic Load Balancer in us-east-2 that backs the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning" for every attempt to POST /api/agents. Because agent creation is the prerequisite step for all three remote-agent checks, none of them could produce any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState), causing a complete contract gap across the entire remote-agents feature. This is an eval-observed infrastructure availability failure scoped to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

[Possible] A network routing or security-group change in us-east-2 severed connectivity between the production-api layer and the swarm ELB, producing a connection-refused or timeout that the API translated into a 502 bad_gateway.
[Less likely] A misconfigured or expired DNS record for the ELB hostname caused the connection attempt to fail before reaching the load balancer.

investigation.summary: The image-generation-stream eval failed because the OpenAI API key used by the eval runner has no remaining credits, causing the upstream image generation call to return a hard error (code: credit_balance_exhausted). The stream terminated with a generation_error frame instead of the required generation_completed frame, so both contract assertions — frameTypes contains "generation_completed" and imageUrlPresent equals true — were violated. The OpenAI API returned HTTP error type "insufficient_quota" with code "credit_balance_exhausted" before image generation could complete. As a result, the SSE stream emitted a generation_error frame and closed without ever emitting a generation_completed frame or an artifact URL, causing both required contract assertions to fail. The failure is localized to the eval runner's OpenAI billing account and the /api/generate/image/stream endpoint under the desktop-release runtime environment; no evidence of a code defect or regression is present.

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-09-16T01:22–01:23Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents endpoint could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents. Because the failure is shared across every sibling check with the same error message and no evidence was collected by any check, the fault is localized to the shared swarm gateway dependency, not to any individual eval's logic.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint that handles /v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every call to POST /api/agents returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", preventing agent creation from completing and leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent. This is an eval-observed infrastructure connectivity failure localized to the swarm gateway; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so broader production impact cannot be confirmed from this packet alone.

Network/security-group misconfiguration between production-api and the swarm ELB: a firewall rule, VPC peering change, or security group update could have severed connectivity from the production-api service to the ELB in us-east-2 at the time of the run.

Transient swarm gateway restart or deployment: the gateway may have been mid-deployment or restarting at the time of the eval run, causing a temporary but complete 502 window across all three checks (which ran within ~22 seconds of each other).

Eval infrastructure misconfiguration (lower confidence): if the ELB hostname or routing configuration used by the eval runner was changed, the runner could be targeting a stale or incorrect endpoint — however, the error message originates from the API layer, not the eval runner itself, making this less likely.
